pr_title: backupccl: add dropping incremental backup schedule when dropping full backup schedule
pr_body:
Fixes #87435

Release note (sql change): Previously, whenever a user dropped a scheduled full backup, the corresponding scheduled incremental backup would not be dropped. This change drops the associated scheduled incremental backup when `DROP SCHEDULE` or `DROP SCHEDULES` is called.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/89768)
drive by comment: should we have explicit, user specified input -- aka CASCADE in sql.y -- to trigger auto drop behavior?

issue_context.title: backupccl: dropping a full backup schedule should automatically drop an incremental schedule
issue_context.body:
Today, when we drop a full schedule we do not drop its dependant incremental schedule. This allows the incremental backup schedule to continue building on the same full backup indefinitely. While we have made backup and restore a lot more scalable to long incremental chains over the past few releases, and unbounded chain of incremental backups is not a spot we want customers to find themselves in. If the chain is beyond our scale limits of restore, this essentially renders the backup useless.

In 22.2 we will also be shipping `ALTER SCHEDULE` which will allows users to alter existing schedules, therefore negating the need to drop and recreate another schedule to tweak a configuration or recurrence. To this effect we propose that a `DROP SCHEDULE` on a schedule corresponding to a full backup, will also drop its dependant incremental schedule. Note, dropping an incremental schedule will **not** result in its parent full schedule being dropped. This is intuitive because a user may want to stop taking incremental backups for numerous reasons.

Jira issue: CRDB-19347
